newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Twenty hurt in Argentine privatization protest.
newsitem.headline: Twenty hurt in Argentine privatization protest.

text.p: Twenty people were hurt in clashes Monday between police and unionists protesting against industry privatisation plans in the central Argentine city of Mendoza, police and union officials said.

Riots broke out when police using water cannons and tear gas stopped 300 workers from entering the provincial Congress, where the Senate had just passed a bill to privatise the province's electricity generator. National television showed protesters pelting Congress with sticks and stones.

Local authorities said most of the injured were police officers. They said the police had acted correctly to defend Congress, and Mendoza Governor Jorge Lopez blamed the riots on "a few people who carry the seeds of violence within."

The country's Peronist government has privatised industry across the board since President Carlos Menem came to power in 1989. Trade unions blame his reforms for the rise in unemployment to 17.3 percent by last year, versus seven percent back in 1989.
